reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 21. Nay or No: 17. Not Voting: 0. Present or other: 2. Of 38 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 37 (97%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 208 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards (H RES 1498)
votes.plain_language: This resolution censures Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A Yea votes to censure him. A Nay votes not to.

lobbying.bill_title: In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards.

votes.question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. This vote would have delayed that bill until the Commerce Secretary published a report on how trade fights with Canada and China, and the war in Iran, affect fishing costs and seafood prices. A Yea would have added that delay; a Nay rejected it.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Passage — PROOF Act (H R 10326)
votes.plain_language: This bill requires states to give the Justice Department information it needs to investigate fraud in Medicaid, food assistance, cash welfare, and certain other federal programs, and it limits that data to law-enforcement use. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
votes.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Value Over Cost Act (H R 1118)
votes.plain_language: This bill specifies that contracts and orders under the multiple award schedule program of the General Services Administration may be evaluated on best value, rather than lowest overall cost, if the GSA determines that to be in the best interests of the federal government. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act (H R 8823)
votes.bill_title: Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act
votes.plain_language: This bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Labor to suspend payments under the federal workers’ compensation program to certain providers convicted of fraud. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Condemning actors seeking to defraud the U.S. Government, and expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that government-wide fraud and improper payment prevention reforms will meaningfully improve the financial prosperity of the U.S., and that Federal program eligibility should be verified before payment (H RES 1335)
votes.bill_title: Condemning actors seeking to defraud the United States Government, and expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that governmentwide fraud and improper payment prevention reforms will meaningfully improve the financial prosperity of the United States, and that Federal program eligibility should be verified before payment.
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns the actions of those seeking to defraud the U.S. government. A Yea agrees to the resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act (H R 8464)
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes requirements to prevent fraudulent or improper payments from federal programs. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act (H R 8464)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 8464 (Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act) establishes requirements to prevent fraudulent or improper payments from federal programs. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act (H R 8312)
votes.plain_language: This bill assigns improper-payment prevention and spending-transparency functions to the Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service, creates an Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery within Treasury, and requires Treasury data-sharing agreements with other agencies and allowable private entities to prevent fraud and improper payments. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Federal Fraud Prevention Workforce Training Act (H R 8428)
votes.bill_title: Federal Fraud Prevention Workforce Training Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget and the Department of the Treasury to establish and maintain a mandatory antifraud and improper payment prevention training program for federal employees whose roles involve federal financial assistance or oversight of federal programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Information Quality Assurance Act (H R 6329)
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget to revise federal agency guidelines for disseminating or using influential information or evidence, meaning information an agency can reasonably determine has a clear and substantial impact on important public actions or private sector decisions. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act (S 1383)
votes.bill_title: Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill carries the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE America Act) as amended in the Senate; it requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to vote in federal elections. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Commit — Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act (S 1383)
votes.bill_title: Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: As amended in the Senate, S. 1383 carries the SAVE America Act, which requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to vote in federal elections. A motion to commit, like a motion to recommit, is the minority's last formal chance to send the bill to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it to committee; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025 (H J RES 142)
votes.bill_title: Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025.
votes.plain_language: This joint resolution reinstates provisions of District of Columbia tax law to conform with federal tax law. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

Meals on Wheels does extraordinary work making sure our Granite State neighbors have access to nutritious meals and the care and connection they deserve. Thank you to everyone who works to make sure no Granite Stater is left behind.

Learn more about opportunities to volunteer with @MOW_HC this holiday season here: https://t.co/EumPrV1oom

It was great to welcome students and teachers from Sunapee Middle High School to the People's House!

Veterans are ready to get to work together and to continue serving the American people. From fighting to end this reckless war in Iran to reining in these chaotic tariffs and trade wars, we are going to deliver affordability through accountability. https://t.co/NaktIj3tKw

Today, President Trump once again called for my prosecution. Why? For restating a bedrock principle of American law that every American servicemember swears an oath to honor: in the United States of America, we follow lawful orders, and lawful orders only.

A grand jury of ordinary citizens already rejected this case — an outrageous abuse of presidential power and genuine waste of taxpayer dollars.

The American people deserve leaders who are working for them to lower costs and crack down on corruption — not more grandstanding and threats from President Trump.

These threats will not deter, distract, intimidate, or silence me. I swore an oath to our Constitution, and I will never stop honoring it by doing my job.

🚨Good news from the People’s House! We passed the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act AND are welcoming nearly 80 veterans to the 120th Congress. Excited to keep working and delivering for New Hampshire.🇺🇸 https://t.co/y8Oe7UV0zA

Row after row, each flag marks a life given in service to something greater than ourselves: a son or daughter, a parent, a neighbor who answered the call.

This Veterans Day, we honor everyone who has worn our nation's uniform, remember those we've lost, and recommit to keeping faith with our veterans and their families. Today and every day. 🇺🇸

You don't have to wait until you're old enough to vote to make a difference in your community. It was so inspiring to join NH Civics' We the Future Student Civics Summit at Saint Anselm College to hear from young Granite Staters about the issues that matter to them.
 
From asking tough questions to listening across differences, these students are already putting democracy into action. Our future is in good hands when young people are willing to show up, speak out, and take responsibility for the communities they call home.

A cleaner, more affordable energy future is taking shape right here in Jaffrey! Loved celebrating the start of this use of public land: a community solar farm, which transforms a former landfill into a source of clean energy and lower electricity bills for hundreds of Granite State households. This is what happens when local leaders, New Hampshire businesses, and neighbors come together to deliver real relief.

Thank you to @revisionsolar, Blue Haven Solar, and the amazing people of the Town of Jaffrey who made this possible.

Ski season is right around the corner in the Granite State. So great to spend the afternoon at @patspeak in Henniker for their annual Oktoberfest and Ski & Snowboard Sale, celebrating the start of another winter season with local families and outdoor enthusiasts.

Thank you to https://t.co/1DlSkPTpCv

When the alarm sounds, Keene's firefighters run in. Grateful to Chief Greg Seymour, Captain Jeremy LaPlante, and the entire team at the Keene Fire Department for talking with me about firefighter readiness, health, and safety.

Firefighters and first responders have our backs. I'll always have theirs.

Gloria Timmons was the ultimate Nashuan. There was no task too big or too small, and she always showed up for her community. One year after her passing, her legacy of service, kindness, and bringing people together continues to inspire me and our entire city. Nashua is a better place because of Gloria Timmons, and we miss her dearly.

Thank you, Dan and the Nashua Independent, for putting together this beautiful way to honor her memory.💜

Read the article and watch the full video here: 
https://t.co/Kh5lVjAHOX
To the Granite State Ambassadors: thank you for showing the world the best of who we are as a state. I cannot wait to see what we can do together in the 30 years ahead.🇺🇸 https://t.co/mFmeSNpreS

Every time I fly home from our nation's capital and walk off the plane at MHT, there they are: those iconic green shirts. That's how I know I'm home.

For 30 years, the Granite State Ambassadors have shown the world what makes New Hampshire so special: our people. They've trained thousands of volunteers, who give tens of thousands of hours and welcome more than 100,000 visitors every year. You'll find them at our airport, welcome centers, craft fairs and agricultural fairs, and at my favorite store in our state, the State House gift shop (check it out! https://t.co/uudHXRHDTd).

It was a joy to celebrate 30 years of service. Thank you for asking "How can I help?" 100,000 times a year, and for making New Hampshire the best place on earth to visit and call home.

Our veterans have served our country with extraordinary courage and sacrifice. We have a responsibility to keep our promises to them. So happy to join Ralph Mecheau and local veterans at T-BONES in Concord for community conversations about improving access to VA health care, protecting earned benefits, and making housing more affordable.

As a member of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, I'll keep fighting to ensure every Granite State veteran receives the care, benefits, and support they've earned.

Every day, first responders across New Hampshire answer the call to keep our communities safe, often putting their own lives on the line to protect their neighbors. On National First Responders Day, we honor our firefighters, law enforcement officers, EMTs, paramedics, and emergency dispatchers for their extraordinary courage, sacrifice, and service.

To our first responders and their families: thank you for all you do for the Granite State.🇺🇸

In a trauma emergency, every second counts — and in rural New Hampshire, every mile does too.

I visited Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center, our state's only Level I trauma center, and spent time with the surgeons, nurses, docs, first responders, and emergency teams who get Granite Staters from the worst moment of their lives to the care that saves lives.

That lifeline starts long before the hospital doors: with a volunteer ambulance crew up north, a community ER, a DHART flight crew. Every link has to hold.

I'm fighting to make sure it does — by backing the people who do this work and protecting the rural hospitals and EMS services they rely on. Your zip code should never decide whether you survive.

Every Granite Stater deserves access to fresh, healthy food, and our local farmers deserve to thrive.

Great conversation at Kearsarge Food Hub in Bradford with farmers, food pantry leaders, and community partners about fighting food insecurity, supporting family farms, and getting more locally grown food onto our neighbors’ tables. Thank you to Hanna, Lauren, and the entire team for bringing us together!

New Hampshire’s family farms are the backbone of our communities, but rising costs, workforce shortages, and federal red tape are making it harder to keep them running.

Great conversation in Francestown with local farmers about the challenges they face and what Congress can do to help.

Thank you to Bob and Judy for hosting us at your amazing Bob’s Chocolate Cafe!

Great to be at @SaintAnselm with the @NECouncil and leaders from across New Hampshire, including @AARPNH and the @alzheimersmanh, to hear directly from you, answer your questions, and discuss protecting Social Security, supporting NH caregivers, cracking down on corruption across our government, ending President Trump’s war in Iran, and delivering for Granite Staters.

When Granite Staters call for help, our law enforcement officers answer. Grateful to meet with the NH Association of Chiefs of Police to hear directly about the challenges they face. I'll keep fighting to get our officers the resources, training, and support they need to keep our communities safe.

What an honor to help cut the ribbon on Predictive Monitor's new headquarters today, right here in my hometown of Nashua!

Laurie and John Masiello have spent decades protecting the medicines and research that patients and families count on. They built Masy BioServices from the ground up, and now they're growing Predictive Monitor here at home.

Laurie, John, and the whole Predictive Monitor team: I'm so proud of what you've built, and it meant a lot to celebrate with you today. Congratulations on this next chapter. I can't wait to see what you do next!

The future of New Hampshire agriculture and food is in good hands! 🐄

I loved meeting the young Granite Staters of NH 4-H at the Sandwich Fair. They spend all year caring for their animals, and their pride and hard work were on full display in every barn and show ring. Every 4-H member pledges their head, heart, hands, and health to their club, community, country, and world, and I saw that pledge in action.

I also met so many of the people who make this fair so special: the local vendors, crafters, food makers, and small businesses who who put in long hours to share their work with their neighbors.

The costs of fuel, feed, equipment, and everyday living keep climbing, and it gets harder every year to keep a farm or small business in the family.

I'll keep fighting so our family farms and family-owned small businesses can thrive for generations to come. 🇺🇸

Fall in New Hampshire is in full swing! 🎃🍁

Great to be at the Milford Pumpkin Festival on Sunday, celebrating the season with neighbors, families, and friends. Thank you to everyone who makes this beloved Granite State tradition so special! https://t.co/dnjeVDVhVv

As the great-granddaughter of New Hampshire family farmers, I know how important our farms are to the health of our communities, our economy, and our way of life.

On National Farmers Day, I want to thank every farmer and farm family across our state and our country. I'll keep fighting to make sure our family farms can thrive for generations to come. 🇺🇸

No better place to start the week than the Sandwich Fair, a hometown tradition with roots back to 1886 that's still run by neighbors and powered by volunteers! 🎡🐂

It was awesome to see families reuniting, NH 4-H kids showing their animals, local vendors shining, and the whole community coming together.

🙏 Thank you to Bryan Peaslee & the Sandwich Fair Association for the countless hours that go into keeping this tradition alive year after year!

Head Start is about more than early education. It's about giving kids the tools to succeed and families the support they need. I saw that firsthand in Nashua this week. I'll keep fighting to protect the quality early education Granite State families deserve. https://t.co/CW1fsVgAeL

We have always been a state where making things that matter is core to our DNA. 

It was an honor to join NH MEP's Annual Summit to celebrate our incredible manufacturers, small businesses, and the next generation of innovators. Thank you for the heroic work you do for our state. You are helping build the future of manufacturing right here in New Hampshire.

Every child in New Hampshire deserves a safe place to learn, grow, and get a fair shot at success. Head Start helps deliver on that promise while helping hardworking parents stay in the workforce and provide for their families. At a time when Granite Staters are struggling to find and afford childcare, Secretary Robert F. Kennedy is brazenly trying to dismantle Head Start, and make it harder for kids and families to get the care they need. That is unacceptable. I’m fighting to protect Head Start and make quality childcare more affordable and accessible for New Hampshire families.

Every kid in New Hampshire deserves a fair shot, a world-class education, and a whole lot of love. 

Loved visiting Head Start in Nashua, reading with students, and hearing from incredible Head Start educators and the amazing team at CAP Hillsborough and Rockingham. I'll keep fighting to deliver for our early childhood educators and Head Start and make world-class early childhood education a reality for every family in our state.

I had a great meeting this week with our Education Commissioner Caitlin Davis and Career Development Administrator Chrissy Vander Hook to discuss bringing more federal resources to support New Hampshire's public schools and CTE programs. Public education is the ultimate engine and guardrail of our democracy, and I’m fighting with everything I’ve got to support our public schools across New Hampshire. 

We also took time to write holiday cards to our deployed servicemembers as part of Dr. Laura Landerman-Garber's Holiday Cards 4 Our Military – NH Challenge. A meaningful way to show our gratitude to those serving far from home and remind them that we always have their backs. 🇺🇸

New Hampshire’s mountains, lakes, trails, forests, and farms bring people together—and help veterans heal.

Today I was proud to help introduce the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act with @RepJeffHurd. By helping cover equipment, transportation, and program costs, our bill would help more veterans get outdoors, connect with one another, and strengthen their physical and mental health.

Our veterans have earned this support. Cost shouldn’t stand in their way.

I will be relentless in taking on the private equity companies, the price gouging corporations that are jacking up your costs, and we will fight with everything we've got to restore and reverse these cuts to your healthcare. https://t.co/RKRKgP8sD6

Every Granite Stater with a disability has the right to live, work, and belong in their community. That’s what Section 504 and the Supreme Court’s Olmstead decision guarantee.

A Justice Department memo can’t erase laws Congress passed or overturn Supreme Court precedent. I won’t stop fighting to protect these rights.

Keeping our promises to those who serve doesn’t end when the uniform comes off. Grateful to be back with New Hampshire’s State Veterans Advisory Committee to hear directly from veterans about what’s working, where people are still falling through the cracks, and what more we need to do. Your experience informs my work in Congress — and I’ll always have your back.

October 7, 2023, was the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust. Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists murdered more than 1,200 people — civilians, servicemembers, children, and grandparents — and took 251 innocent people hostage.

Families endured the agony of waiting. This year, at last, every hostage has come home. For some families, that meant a joyful reunion. For others, it meant finally laying a loved one to rest. My heart is with all of them, and with every innocent person whose life has been taken or upended since October 7, 2023.

I will keep working for an enduring peace: one that confronts antisemitism wherever it appears, including here at home; ensures Hamas can never again threaten the people of Israel and innocent civilians; protects Israel’s security and democracy; delivers the humanitarian relief the people of Gaza still urgently need; and builds a future where Israelis and Palestinians alike can live with security, freedom, dignity, and hope.

From clearing snow to maintaining the roads we rely on every day, local public works crews keep New Hampshire moving. Great to visit the Northwood Highway Department and hear directly from town officials and DPW Foreman Mack Grimmett and Selectboard Vice Chair Matt Frye and Town Manager Neil Irvine about the essential work needed to serve their community.

Thank you to the whole team for all you do for Northwood and our state!

Behind every healthcare number is a person. A mom staring at a stack of bills. A student waiting months for mental health care. A veteran skipping appointments because the drive is too far.

I joined @ProtectCareNH in Concord because we have a healthcare crisis in this country — and I’ll be relentless in fighting to lower costs, protect Medicaid, and make sure every Granite Stater can get the care they need.

Our firefighters show up for us on our hardest days. We need to show up for them.

Thank you to Chief Mark Tetreault, the whole team from the Northwood Fire Rescue Department, Northwood Selectboard Vice Chair Matt Frye, and Northwood Town Manager Neil Irvine and for showing me around and talking with me about how we can work together to keep this community safe.
We are who we are by way of memory — and our state will always remember what Dan MacDonald has done for us.🇺🇸 https://t.co/1naUTs4HD6

Thank you for coming to our nation's capital to see our government up close. Your questions were thoughtful and your ideas were truly inspiring. The future of our democracy is in https://t.co/nVIJ1Wqno2

Veterans are ready to get to work together and to continue serving the American people. From fighting to end this reckless war in Iran to reining in these chaotic tariffs and trade wars, we are going to deliver affordability through accountability. https://t.co/NaktIj3tKw

Today, President Trump once again called for my prosecution. Why? For restating a bedrock principle of American law that every American servicemember swears an oath to honor: in the United States of America, we follow lawful orders, and lawful orders only.

A grand jury of ordinary citizens already rejected this case — an outrageous abuse of presidential power and genuine waste of taxpayer dollars.

The American people deserve leaders who are working for them to lower costs and crack down on corruption — not more grandstanding and threats from President Trump.

These threats will not deter, distract, intimidate, or silence me. I swore an oath to our Constitution, and I will never stop honoring it by doing my job.

funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
